why: MI-280 unit U1. Adds a MERGEABILITY dimension to the PR-queue watcher so a pull request that is green on every check and impossible to merge stops rendering identically to one that is ready. Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list: scripts/ops/**, .github/workflows/**, tests/** and docs/claude/work/** only — no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path, no strategy config, no risk cap, no live-VM runtime file. R12 does NOT apply and that was checked rather than assumed: neither scripts/ops/pr_queue_latency.py nor .github/workflows/pr-queue-watch.yml appears in check_pr_landing.py::LANDING_MACHINERY, and the new scripts/ops/pr_mergeability.py is not a landing route — it grades a PR's mergeability and can neither open, arm, nor merge anything. The watcher's blast radius is unchanged: it reads the open-PR list plus one payload per PR and writes one generated JSON receipt under docs/claude/work/; it never merges, closes, un-drafts or comments on a pull request. MEASURED BASIS, population stated: the COMPLETE open-PR queue of 5 on 2026-09-12, read via mcp__github__pull_request_read — #11738 (Tier-2, operator-approved) and #11859 (the manager's own status push) are both 5-of-5 green AND mergeable_state 'dirty', the first for 12h+ and the second within 20 minutes of being opened, while the deployed watcher grades them 'waiting' and 'active' respectively and its exit code on that queue is 0. VERIFICATION: 10 planted defects, 10 caught, positive control quiet on restore — and the FIRST mutation run caught 9 of 10, the miss being a cancelled+dirty case that did not exist until the run found its absence. 35 pytest cases, three of which break a load-bearing predicate in isolation and assert the suite goes red. run_guards.py --base main on committed state: PASS 71 / FAIL 1 / SKIP 23, the single failure being this declaration's own absence.
